record.d: Hand-cut, hand-stitched leather footstool and floor cushion made in the medinas of Fez and Marrakech from Moroccan-tanned leather, used as footrest, seat or low table.
record.dt: round or rectangular · vegetable-tanned leather · embroidered or plain

items.why: Origin version of Ottoman (pouf is already an alias of the kind).

record.d: Plain turned-post ladder-back chair with a woven seat, a core business of the New Lebanon Shaker community by the 1860s.
record.dt: side chair or rocker · several sizes · woven seat

items.why: Ambiguous resolved: the style goes to VE, but the Shaker chair is a named, bought and auctioned piece, so an archetype under Dining chair (rockers could be a version later).

Ambiguous resolved: a period style spanning every furniture form; no single ware is named by it. Individual forms (e.g. horseshoe-back armchair) could be added later as archetypes from their own pages.

record.a: Syrian mother-of-pearl table · Damascene inlaid table
record.d: Small table or pedestal of wood inlaid with mother-of-pearl and bone, made in workshops on Straight Street, Damascus, from at least the 1890s and still in c. 2010.

items.why: Origin version of Side table; the inlay technique stays in VE. Page names no individual workshop.

record.a: thuya wood box · Moroccan marquetry box
record.d: Box of fragrant thuya wood inlaid with ebony, walnut, citrus wood, mother-of-pearl and bone, made in the woodworkers' souk (Skala de la Ville) of Essaouira.

items.why: Origin version of a box; page names the souk and co-ops but no individual workshop.

record.d: Carved table of Kashmir walnut wood made in Jammu and Kashmir, a craft registered as a geographical indication in 2007–08 that also makes jewellery boxes and trays.

items.why: GI-protected; the page names tables, boxes and trays, so the table goes here as an origin version (boxes/trays could follow in B4/B5).

record.d: Carved wooden furniture from Jepara regency, Central Java, home to 348 large furniture firms, whose administration patented 99 characteristic carving motifs in 2009.

items.why: Origin-protected furniture; the page names no single form, so a kind (could alternatively be a regional maker division).

record.d: Flat screen of panels of turned wooden lattice above a solid base, as in an 18th-century Egyptian example at the Metropolitan Museum.
record.dt: open or dense lattice · stained, painted or plain

items.why: Interior mashrabiya screens are made and sold as room dividers; the architectural window form and lattice craft stay in VE.
